q: ID3 searches the space of trees using:
options: Greedy top-down search with no backtracking
explain: It chooses the best attribute at each node and never reconsiders.

q: ID3 returns a leaf with the most common label when:
options: No attributes remain but the examples still disagree
All examples have the same label
The gain of an attribute is high
explain: With nothing left to test, the best available answer is the majority label.

q: In the 14-day data, which attribute does ID3 test under Outlook = Sunny?
explain: Humidity has gain 0.971 on the Sunny days, which is a perfect split.
Wind splits the Rain days perfectly, with gain 0.971.

q: Which attribute never appears in the tree learned from the 14-day data?
explain: Temp is never the best choice at any node, so ID3 leaves it out.

q: What is the entropy of the 5 Sunny days (2 Yes, 3 No)? Give 3 decimal places.
How many leaves does the tree learned from the 14-day data have?
explain: Overcast gives 1 leaf, Humidity gives 2, and Wind gives 2.

q: Why is a 'Day number' attribute a problem for plain information gain?
options: It splits the data into pure single-example groups, so its gain is very high but it cannot generalise
It has a gain of zero
It cannot be turned into a branch
explain: Every branch is pure, so gain is maximal, yet the attribute tells us nothing about a new day.
